mainEntity.name: Will Kuma work on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kuma works on iPhones running iOS 18 or later. The special iPhone Duo layouts need iOS 27.1 or later. You can use the timer, practice history, written guide, and widgets on other supported iPhones, too.

mainEntity.name: Does Kuma work on iPhone Duo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Kuma adjusts as you open, fold, or turn your iPhone Duo. When fully open, Kuma sits beside your timer. When half-open on a table, Kuma appears above the timer controls. These layouts need iOS 27.1 or later.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an account or an Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can meditate on your iPhone without signing in. Apple Watch, cloud backup, and Apple Health are optional. The Watch app needs watchOS 11 or later.

mainEntity.name: How do I use Kuma on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Install Kuma on the Apple Watch paired with your iPhone. Open Kuma on your Watch and choose how you’ll meditate and for how long. Tap Begin. You can pause or finish from your Watch, too. Your Watch needs watchOS 11 or later. Completed meditations appear in your iPhone history when the devices reconnect.

mainEntity.name: How do I use Kuma with Apple Health?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Kuma, open Settings → Apple Health. Choose Save to Mindful Minutes if you’d like to record your meditation time in Apple Health. For optional heart-rate readings, turn on Heart rate reports and Measure on Apple Watch, then allow the access Apple asks for. With Watch measurement enabled, beginning a meditation on your iPhone can start recording on your nearby Watch. Readings may take time to appear and depend on what your devices record. Heart rate doesn’t tell you how well you meditated, and Kuma doesn’t assess it for medical purposes.

mainEntity.name: How do I add a Kuma widget?

acceptedAnswer.text: A widget is a small view of Kuma that lives on your Home Screen. Touch and hold your iPhone’s Home Screen. Choose Edit → Add Widget and search for Kuma. Pick a small or medium widget. To change its colors, open Kuma’s Settings → Widget appearance and choose Sunshine, Night Gold, or Match System. Your iPhone decides when widgets update, so changes may take a little time to appear.

Kuma’s community is other real people who have meditated in Kuma. The animal images are avatars members choose to represent themselves. Open Community from Log or Settings, sign in with Apple, and choose a community name and one of 55 animal avatars. Joining is optional; signing in alone doesn’t make you visible. After you have joined and meditated, you can see other members who have meditated in Kuma at any time. This isn’t a live group session. Members see your chosen name, animal, and that you’ve meditated; your session times, durations, reflections, and Health data stay private. You can leave anytime.

mainEntity.name: What kind of meditation is Kuma for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kuma gives you a timer for practicing on your own, whether you’re sitting, walking, standing, or lying down. There’s also a written guide with teachings and reflections to explore. The guide works without an internet connection.

mainEntity.name: What if I miss a day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then you can practice again when you’re able. You can choose a weekly aspiration that fits your life, and change it as your circumstances change. Even a short meditation counts. If you enjoy keeping a daily streak, you can choose that in Settings.

Kuma is the bear keeping you company as you practice. His round, legless shape is inspired by Japanese Daruma dolls, traditionally associated with perseverance. The inspiration behind Kuma Daruma dolls are inspired by Bodhidharma, a Buddhist teacher. The circle on Kuma’s belly echoes the ensō, a circle painted with a brush in Zen art. His white color is a nod to the upāsaka, a lay Buddhist practitioner. The Pāli Canon describes white-clad lay followers practicing amid everyday life.
